newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbian IMR to boost tractor sales to Egypt, Africa.
newsitem.headline: Serbian IMR to boost tractor sales to Egypt, Africa.

text.p: Serbia's tractor producer Industrija Motora Rakovica (IMR) expects to earn more than $8 million over the next eight months from sales to Egypt, the Belgrade daily Politika wrote on Friday.

"IMR will export 1,200 tractors to the Egyptian firm Universal from Beni Suef over the next seven to eight months worth $8.5 million," the manufacturer's general manager Vaso Pindovic was quoted as saying.

It will deliver a further $2.5 million worth of tractors by the end of 1997 to Nasco, one of the largest Egyptian state companies, and expects to collect a total of $15 million from the two Egyptian firms by the end of 1998, Pindovic said.
IMR won its export deals with the Egyptian companies after a tough competition with Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Romania, Poland and China, he added.
Egypt is seen as a promising export market, after announcing plans to increase its crop area to 12.7 percent from 5.5 percent of its territory.

Besides substantial ongoing deals with Egypt, IMR, which has recently been granted 1.5 million German marks for export sales by the Serbian Development Fund, also plans to boost exports to other African states.

IMR has exported 215 tractors worth $200,000 to Botswana, Zimbabwe, Tanzania and South Africa in 1997 and expects to renew deliveries to these countries from September. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
